name: X-linked Severe Congenital Neutropenia

criteria.description: Absolute neutrophil count (ANC) persistently below 0.5 x 10^9/L
Recurrent severe bacterial infections starting in infancy
Absence of ELANE gene mutations with confirmed mutation in the WAS gene (Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome gene)
Bone marrow examination showing maturation arrest at the promyelocyte/myelocyte stage
X-linked pattern of inheritance with affected male relatives

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Persistent severe neutropenia with recurrent bacterial infections and identification of pathogenic WAS gene mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential to confirm diagnosis and differentiate from other forms of congenital neutropenia.

laboratory: Bone marrow biopsy showing maturation arrest at promyelocyte stage
imaging: Radiographs showing osteomyelitis or bone infections in advanced cases
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in the WAS gene confirming X-linked inheritance
other: Family history consistent with X-linked pattern
Response to granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) therapy

distinguishingFeatures: Similar neutropenia but different genetic etiology
ELANE mutations common but clinical course differs

redFlags: Severe recurrent bacterial infections in male infants
Persistent absolute neutrophil count below 0.5 x10^9/L
Family history of early infant deaths or severe infections in males
references: Dale DC, et al. Severe congenital neutropenia: diagnosis, molecular basis, and clinical management. Hematology Am Soc Hematol Educ Program. 2013.
Horwitz MS, et al. Severe congenital neutropenia caused by mutations in the WAS gene. Blood. 2007.
